answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it can trade, with every transaction linked to one continuous identity thread of past behaviour. Creating one credible identity is cheap, but spawning thousands means locking stake for each and maintaining a separate, verifiable history for every thread, so the cost scales linearly while the benefit of a fake flood does not. Attackers who try to cross that gap face a canyon of upfront cost: sybils that misbehave lose their stake, while honest agents keep trading and gradually earn their deposit back.
